# Repository Instructions

This file is the entry point for agent instructions in this repository.
Workflows and policies live in the documents under `docs/agents/`; the domain
vocabulary lives in `CONTEXT.md` at the root.

## Testing and Verification

Tests are part of the specification. Write the failing test first at the
spec's pre-agreed seams and make it green with the minimal change — red
before green, one seam, one test, one slice per cycle — per the build
discipline in [docs/agents/issue-tracker.md](docs/agents/issue-tracker.md).
Test-after is reserved for glue and wiring, UI verified by a manual test plan,
and throwaway prototypes. During implementation and review, run the focused
checks recorded under Agent skills for the changed areas and their immediate
contracts; the epic gate recorded there is reserved for the final integrated
epic commit before acceptance and closure.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Gitea issues, driven by the `gitea-issues` helpers.
See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Canonical role names mapped to this tracker's label strings.
See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

single layout: CONTEXT.md and ADRs live per `docs/agents/domain.md`.

### Work queue

Priority lives in the `type/roadmap` issue's ordered queue; see `docs/agents/queue.md`.

### Working standards

Docs and tests are first-class artifacts; the tracker is the queue, repository
documents the durable memory. Read the issue's epic and related issues
before planning; build test-first at the spec's pre-agreed seams; record each
change's documentation disposition and the evidence behind its merge; commands
presented as runnable must be ready to run as written. See
`docs/agents/standards.md`.

### Focused checks

`uv run --locked pytest tests/<area>`

Run on the exact current head during implementation and review follow-ups;
any later change makes this evidence stale.

### Epic gate

`make check`

The complete gate, reserved for final epic acceptance — run once on the exact
integrated commit. On an execution host, run it as
`scripts/execution_host.py gate`, which runs `make check` in a dedicated
checkout at the staged checkout's exact commit and keeps a receipt (see
`docs/runbooks/portable-execution-host.md`, "Run the gate").

# Working Standards

The philosophies every session in this repository works under. The
`## Agent skills` block in the agent instructions carries the one-line rules;
this document is the authority behind them and is safe to extend per repo.

## Documentation and tests are first-class artifacts

Code may be replaced, but durable decisions, behavior, and lessons must remain
recoverable from focused documentation and verification artifacts. A future
agent with no conversation history should be able to determine:

- what the system currently does;
- which behavior is only proposed, not implemented;
- why important architectural decisions were made;
- how to verify implemented behavior;
- which earlier approaches are retained only for context (`docs/historical/`).

## Documents versus the issue tracker

The issue tracker is the queue for actionable work and holds the transient
working context of one change; repository documents are the durable memory. A
closed issue thread is not a supported reference for current behavior. When an
issue resolves a term or a decision, record it in `CONTEXT.md` or an ADR
rather than leaving it only in the thread; an idea too valuable to lose and
not actionable enough to be an issue belongs in the domain documents, not in
an issue comment.

Before addressing an issue, read the issue with its comments, every other
issue in its epic, and the issues in related epics. Confirm scope, boundaries,
and dependencies before planning.

## Writing current-truth documents

`CONTEXT.md` and the ADRs describe what the system does, in present tense, as
a contract — not a narrative of the change that produced them.

- Test every sentence carrying an issue reference by deleting the number: if
  the sentence stays true, the reference was decoration and goes; if it stops
  making sense, rewrite it as a statement of current behavior. ADRs keep
  their references — they are decision records.
- ADRs are immutable. Never rewrite a decided ADR; mark it superseded and
  record the replacement decision in a new ADR that links back.
- State uncertainty explicitly, and label proposed behavior as proposed.
- When verified behavior lands, reconcile `CONTEXT.md` and the ADRs in the
  same iteration. Never document behavior that does not exist yet.

## Historical records

`docs/historical/` holds superseded designs, archived handoffs, and
development records. Use it to understand how the project arrived at its
current state; never treat it as current behavior. When reconciling
documents after verified behavior lands, move superseded context that still
explains decisions or discarded alternatives to `docs/historical/` rather
than deleting it. Decisions themselves supersede through the ADR mechanism,
not by moving.

## Documentation disposition

The implementing session records one documentation disposition on the issue
or pull request before completion — in an issue comment on trackers without a
pull-request template. On Gitea, `/cleanup` blocks the merge without one.

`CONTEXT.md` and ADRs are created lazily (see `docs/agents/domain.md`): a
change that resolves no new term or decision records `not_required` rather
than forcing a document into existence.

- **updated** — verified behavior was reconciled into `CONTEXT.md` and the
  ADRs as present-tense contracts;
- **not_required** — the change made no durable behavioral or architectural
  difference; say why in one line;
- **deferred** — documentation work remains; normal completion waits unless
  the owner explicitly accepts the deferral;
- **blocked** — documentation cannot be reconciled because implementation or
  verification evidence is insufficient.

## Build discipline

Tests are part of the specification. Write the failing test first at the
spec's pre-agreed seams and make it green with the minimal change — red
before green, one seam, one test per cycle. Test-after is reserved for glue
and wiring, UI verified by a manual test plan, and throwaway prototypes.

## Verification cadence

During implementation and review follow-ups, run the focused checks for the
changed areas and their immediate contracts or consumers, on the exact
current head. A later code, test, configuration, or documentation change
invalidates the affected evidence and requires those checks again.

Reserve the complete gate declared as the epic gate for the final integrated
epic commit, before epic acceptance and closure. Existing successful CI
satisfies it only when bound to that exact commit. Run a repository-wide
suite earlier only when explicitly requested, when a failure cannot be
localized, or when a change to shared test infrastructure, root
configuration, or a foundational contract has an unbounded blast radius — and
state the reason before starting it.

Do not delete, weaken, skip, or consolidate tests solely to reduce runtime.
Pruning is legitimate only with evidence that the coverage is obsolete or
redundant, the behavior preserved at the lowest faithful layer, and the
verification documentation updated.
When automated coverage is not practical for an enduring contract, record a
repeatable manual procedure and its expected result beside that contract.

## Merge evidence

Every pull request carries the evidence that caused it to be merged, recorded
before the merge: screenshots for a visible interface, brief command output
for command-line behavior, the focused checks that passed and the exact head
they ran against when the effect is not observable through any interface.
Attribute a reported observation to whoever made it rather than presenting it
as independently verified, and never attach evidence that was not examined.
An unrecorded verification did not happen.

## Commands given to the user

A command presented as runnable must be ready to run as written — no
unresolved placeholder such as `/absolute/path/to/...`, `<your-token>`, or an
unassigned `$VALUE`. When a value cannot be known while drafting, give the

content.content:
# Harness Evaluation

This context defines the language used to compare coding-agent harness and model combinations as complete experimental systems.

## Language

**Experimental arm**:
A fully specified harness-model-provider configuration whose identity includes its protocol, reasoning level, runtime policy, and other behavior-affecting settings.
_Avoid_: Model, harness, configuration

**Standard arm**:
A product-native, single-agent experimental arm eligible for Stage A screening; Codex, OpenCode, and Claude Code identities are separate standard arms even when they share a model or research policy.
_Avoid_: Model-only arm, generic competitor, RelayView arm

**Trial**:
One attempt by one experimental arm on one frozen task in a fresh task environment.
_Avoid_: Run, benchmark

**Admission**:
The deterministic conformance decision that an experimental arm satisfies its declared contract and may receive benchmark tasks.
_Avoid_: Smoke test, setup check

**Pair validation**:
The pre-benchmark proof that one newly implemented experimental arm can attempt one predeclared repository-fix task through admission, execution, and independent scoring.
_Avoid_: Benchmark result, conformance matrix

**Unsupported arm**:
An experimental arm that cannot satisfy a required part of its contract and therefore cannot be admitted.
_Avoid_: Failed trial, zero score

**Infrastructure-failed trial**:
A trial that cannot produce a valid capability result because infrastructure outside the agent's task-solving behavior failed.
_Avoid_: Failed task, zero score

**Native sandbox failure**:
An error from the sandbox's exec transport or its sandbox-tools server while a native agent process is being started or streamed. Before it is recorded, the server's state is kept and every process the agent started is stopped, so capture and verification see a quiescent workspace. The trial is then an infrastructure-failed trial with error code `native_sandbox_failed`, or `native_process_lost` for a lost native process, keeping the stream collected so far. An agent that cannot be confirmed stopped still stops the cohort.
_Avoid_: Agent crash, harness crash

**Lost native process**:
A native sandbox failure in which the sandbox-tools server no longer knows the agent's process: it answers `No job found`, or stops answering polls. The process may still be running, orphaned by a replaced server, so its terminal state is unknown. Its error code is `native_process_lost`; it is never treated as the agent finishing, failing or timing out.
_Avoid_: Agent crash, timeout

**Agent user**:
The unprivileged user `agent` that runs every Stage A native agent's process tree, in dispatch, admission and image qualification alike. It has the UID and GID of the operator who runs the harness, who also owns the research socket and the mounted credentials, and those numbers resolve to `agent` even where the image already has an account with them. It owns the sanitized workspace and its arm's home, holds no capabilities, and cannot signal the root sandbox-tools server or reach its state in `/run/sandbox-tools`. Root runs sanitization, capture, export and the verifier.
_Avoid_: Sandbox user, non-root mode

**Capability result**:
A verifier outcome produced after an admitted arm received the task and its task-solving behavior was validly observed.
_Avoid_: Run result

**Evaluation backend**:
The local orchestration and isolation system that provisions trial environments, invokes harnesses, runs verifiers, and records evidence; it is the measuring instrument, not an experimental arm.
_Avoid_: Harness, agent

**Execution host registry**:
The reviewed, committed `hosts/<host_id>.json` entries that state each evaluation host's nonsecret identity: hostname, owner console-verified ED25519 host-key fingerprint, evaluation Docker endpoint, storage mount and data root, vault, execution root and image-store lock. A machine is an execution host only when its hostname and host key verify as an entry with a recorded fingerprint; an entry whose fingerprint is pending is registered but admits nothing. Host-key proofs, the Docker endpoint and data root behind profile observations and probes, Stage A storage policy, mount and lock, Brave's vault, and Docker selection derive from the entry; the ledger, artifact and credential-database paths an operator supplies do not.
_Avoid_: Host config, inventory, default host

**Research ledger transfer**:
The move of the conserved shared-research ledger directory to another execution host at the identical absolute path its allocation journal names: a quiescent, checksummed export on the source, a byte- and row-verified import that must pass the allocation check at the target, and retirement of the source by renaming it aside, never deleting it. Exactly one host holds a live ledger; a fresh account is never a substitute.
_Avoid_: Ledger copy, account reset, re-provisioning

**Benchmark corpus**:
A versioned, pre-results set of frozen tasks, source and environment revisions, verifiers, exclusions, and selection rationale shared by every admitted experimental arm.
_Avoid_: Benchmark, task list, dataset

**Pilot corpus**:
A small benchmark corpus used to validate one admitted experimental arm and the end-to-end evaluation machinery before comparative experiments; its results do not support cross-arm rankings.
_Avoid_: Comparative benchmark, full benchmark

**Comparative corpus**:
A benchmark corpus selected and frozen for paired evaluation across every admitted experimental arm after the pilot corpus has validated the evaluation machinery.
_Avoid_: Pilot corpus, dataset

**Corpus freeze**:
The binding decision after which a benchmark corpus cannot be changed in place; any post-trial change requires a newly identified corpus and may not be based on capability results.
_Avoid_: Sample, shortlist

**Task archive binding**:
The exact archive commit and manifest, task source and text, reviewed validator, and preserved environment identities selected for a prospective task. A new validator or changed byte requires a new binding and freeze; historical task rows retain their original identities.
_Avoid_: Latest validator, mutable dataset row

**Continuous archive cohort**:
The execution of every block of an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze in schedule order from one ledger, advancing automatically after each clean block under the per-block supervisor and stopping fail-closed otherwise; an identity-preserving Claude enrollment renewal is a recorded operator recovery, and an offline audit of every slot precedes the seal.
_Avoid_: First block, gated continuation, rehearsal cohort

**Freeze publication**:
The step that turns an assembled unsigned Stage A candidate and the owner's separate `stage-a-freeze-approval/1` record into the admitted freeze, its admission directory and the copy at the execution configuration's `freeze_path`. It applies the same approval check as dispatch admission (the exact candidate digest, recorded no later than `frozen_at`, `frozen_at` passed, the window not ended) over retained evidence unchanged since assembly; it never creates, edits or infers an approval and never replaces a published file.
_Avoid_: Signing, auto-approval, freeze regeneration

**Archive plan basis**:
The committed, digest-pinned record of the arms, limits and source policy of the most recent owner-approved Stage A plan, with the source path and SHA-256 of its freeze and approval. An archive cohort plan carries only these values from history; its configuration paths, research account and every account's identity evidence derive from the executing host's own admitted evidence.
_Avoid_: Prior plan copy, template freeze

**Research lease**:
The Brave key the shared-research sidecar reads during a cohort: one private file on the verified `/dev/shm` tmpfs, exported from the executing host's own admitted vault in the same single unlock as the provider credential lease. It is never on persistent disk, is re-exported after every reboot and removed when the cohort is sealed or stopped.
_Avoid_: Credential file, persistent lease

**Provider credential lease**:
The seven arms' provider credentials (Claude setup token, Z.AI and Meta keys, Codex ChatGPT login) for an unattended cohort: one private file each beside the research lease, with a manifest binding each file to the admitted vault's digest. The supervised unit has no terminal and never unlocks the vault; every native credential comes from this lease.
_Avoid_: Provider lease (the research budget's term for a search concurrency slot), credential session

**Provider-contact boundary**:
The point in a native attempt just before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation starts. Everything before it (credential delivery and token lifetime, Claude's token against its receipt, the research service, the sandbox and observer definition) can fail without any provider or research request.
_Avoid_: Trial start, launch

**Pre-contact setup failure**:
A failure an adapter records, by error code, while setting up its native agent inside the evaluation, after the provider-contact boundary but before any tool inventory was approved. The observer forwards no provider request without an approved inventory, so the provider was never contacted. The trial is an infrastructure-failed trial with the adapter's error code, and the cohort continues; a rejected or changed tool inventory still stops it.
_Avoid_: Provider failure, harness crash

**Slot rehearsal**:
The run of the next slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact boundary, torn down before the boundary, with nothing reserved and the research service on a copy of the research state. The launcher rehearses each slot before reserving it, so a failure there stops the cohort with the slot still pending.
_Avoid_: Dry run, preflight

**Archive first block**:
A separately approved comparison of all seven standard arms on one reviewed archived task, with one attempt per arm. Its results form a bounded stop checkpoint and cannot seal the complete Stage A cohort.
_Avoid_: Full cohort, preserved-image diagnostic

**Agent task export**:
The archive view containing only task text and the clean source snapshot. The hidden validator and archive history remain outside the task-solving environment.
_Avoid_: Archive checkout, grading bundle

**Trusted grader export**:
The separate archive view containing the selected test patch, commands, parser, scorer, and shared evaluator. It is consumed only after terminal candidate capture and cannot be mounted into the task-solving environment.
_Avoid_: Agent task export

**Task-input store**:
The sibling directory `<artifacts>.task-inputs` that holds archive-bound task-source trees (agent and grader views, composed verifier workspaces) outside the secret-scanned canonical result root, and beside each composed workspace the exact candidate patch it was composed from. Each tree is named in advance by a canonical export record and bound by a canonical relocation manifest, which also binds that candidate patch by SHA-256; the audit accepts only trees it reproduces exactly from the pinned archive and those patches. No other agent-written bytes live there, and every canonical copy of a candidate is redacted.
_Avoid_: Scanner allow-list, scratch directory, moved-out evidence

**Preserved-image diagnostic**:
A provider-free replay of captured candidate bytes against the selected validator in the exact restored owned image. Its grade receipt retains the archive binding and candidate identity; it is retrospective evidence, not a comparative result or approval.
Later normalization authenticates the complete saved receipt against a separately retained grading-time digest and rejects inconsistent scores, crashed or missing test commands, or official patch identities before recording a fixture result; the parsed log alone decides the score.
_Avoid_: Comparative dispatch

**Workflow checkpoint**:
An immutable candidate observation at a defined boundary within a trial; multiple checkpoints from one workflow are paired measurements, not independent trials.
_Avoid_: Arm, repetition

**Initial candidate**:
The candidate identified by the first accepted clean implementation report before reviewer feedback, regardless of validation outcome.
_Avoid_: First passing patch

**Approved final candidate**:
The settled candidate satisfying current prerequisites with acknowledged review approval for that exact candidate.
_Avoid_: Last patch, terminal candidate

**Terminal candidate**:
The last safely extractable candidate when automatic work ends, including failure or deadline; it does not imply review approval. In Stage A it is the workspace's difference from the sanitized base commit without its build products or its declared dependency paths.
_Avoid_: Approved final candidate

**Build product**:
A file new since the sanitized base commit, whether left untracked or staged or committed by the agent, whose content the base commit does not already hold and that one fixed rule names: an ELF or `ar` file, a libtool wrapper, object or library, an empty automake `.dirstamp`, an automake test result with its log, or any new entry inside an immutable submodule worktree. Stage A capture leaves build products out of the terminal candidate and records them; changes to files tracked at the base commit and every other new file stay in it.
_Avoid_: Junk files, leftovers

**Documented build**:
The build and test commands a task's own repository documents at its frozen revision, pinned per task with the document they come from, its build apart from its tests. Every task whose grader builds into a separate directory has one. When the image pre-configured that directory, the documented build is the build the offline build check requires to succeed and the grader's own build still runs after it, recorded; when the grader configures its own directory, its build is the one that must succeed and the documented build runs after it, recorded.
_Avoid_: In-tree probe, guessed build

**Prepared environment**:
An archive task's second owned image, derived from the image its selected validator grades in, holding the task's dependencies with an offline configuration, its caches and toolchains readable outside `/root`. The agent's sandbox and image qualification run in it; graders never do, keeping the image their validator names. One storage lifecycle loads both images, the grader's first.

**Declared dependency path**:
A dependency folder inside the repository, such as `node_modules`, that a prepared environment keeps, recorded with the SHA-256 of its inventory. The Stage A sanitizer (contract `swe-bench-repository-v2`) keeps exactly these paths, each checked against its hash, and removes every other ignored or untracked file. A declared path is environment, never candidate: no capture or export includes it, and a change to it is never part of a patch.
_Avoid_: Vendored folder, cache (a cache lives outside the repository)

**Offline build check**:
Image qualification's first build, as the agent user, offline, in the prepared environment, on the freshly sanitized workspace: the grader's build commands, or a task's documented build when its grader builds in a pre-configured directory. Every build command must exit 0 within 600 seconds together; its tests then run, recorded and not limited, and the production capture must succeed.

**Unsuitable task**:
A task whose build fails the offline build check: it exits nonzero or outlives its 600-second limit. Qualification stops and names it; it is never given a longer limit.
_Avoid_: Failed task, excluded task (an archive review state about grading)

**Research profile**:
The declared research capability, policy, resources and provenance belonging to one experimental arm.
_Avoid_: Search parity, search quota

**Comparative cohort**:
A frozen collection of experimental arms and shared task, scoring, scheduling and interpretation rules whose results may be analyzed together.
_Avoid_: Run, configuration

**Screening cohort**:
The seven-standard-arm exploratory MultiLang comparative cohort on the frozen Stage A corpus (23 reviewed archive tasks) with one trial per arm-task pair, used for an early direction signal and a predeclared absolute futility disposition; its results are published in full and never pooled with expansion or a repeatability study.
_Avoid_: Pilot XL, preliminary eight-arm run, ranking round, multi-try study

**Futility gate**:
A prospective absolute rule for deciding whether an experimental arm proceeds to expansion; it does not force a fixed number of eliminations and is not a relative rank.
_Avoid_: Bottom arms, cut line, leaderboard elimination

A sealed classification of every scheduled screening slot as resolved, not resolved, capability unknown, or unstarted; the expansion survivor set is derived from this artifact rather than declared independently.
_Avoid_: Survivor list, manual selection, culling note

A separately frozen comparative cohort on new tasks containing every surviving standard arm plus both RelayView arms and standard Pi; its results are not pooled with screening.

# Harness Evaluation

This context defines the language used to compare coding-agent harness and model combinations as complete experimental systems.

## Language

**Experimental arm**:
A fully specified harness-model-provider configuration whose identity includes its protocol, reasoning level, runtime policy, and other behavior-affecting settings.
_Avoid_: Model, harness, configuration

**Standard arm**:
A product-native, single-agent experimental arm eligible for Stage A screening; Codex, OpenCode, and Claude Code identities are separate standard arms even when they share a model or research policy.
_Avoid_: Model-only arm, generic competitor, RelayView arm

**Trial**:
One attempt by one experimental arm on one frozen task in a fresh task environment.
_Avoid_: Run, benchmark

**Admission**:
The deterministic conformance decision that an experimental arm satisfies its declared contract and may receive benchmark tasks.
_Avoid_: Smoke test, setup check

**Pair validation**:
The pre-benchmark proof that one newly implemented experimental arm can attempt one predeclared repository-fix task through admission, execution, and independent scoring.
_Avoid_: Benchmark result, conformance matrix

**Unsupported arm**:
An experimental arm that cannot satisfy a required part of its contract and therefore cannot be admitted.
_Avoid_: Failed trial, zero score

**Infrastructure-failed trial**:
A trial that cannot produce a valid capability result because infrastructure outside the agent's task-solving behavior failed.
_Avoid_: Failed task, zero score

**Native sandbox failure**:
An error from the sandbox's exec transport or its sandbox-tools server while a native agent process is being started or streamed. Before it is recorded, the server's state is kept and every process the agent started is stopped, so capture and verification see a quiescent workspace. The trial is then an infrastructure-failed trial with error code `native_sandbox_failed`, or `native_process_lost` for a lost native process, keeping the stream collected so far. An agent that cannot be confirmed stopped still stops the cohort.
_Avoid_: Agent crash, harness crash

**Lost native process**:
A native sandbox failure in which the sandbox-tools server no longer knows the agent's process: it answers `No job found`, or stops answering polls. The process may still be running, orphaned by a replaced server, so its terminal state is unknown. Its error code is `native_process_lost`; it is never treated as the agent finishing, failing or timing out.
_Avoid_: Agent crash, timeout

**Agent user**:
The unprivileged user `agent` that runs every Stage A native agent's process tree, in dispatch, admission and image qualification alike. It has the UID and GID of the operator who runs the harness, who also owns the research socket and the mounted credentials, and those numbers resolve to `agent` even where the image already has an account with them. It owns the sanitized workspace and its arm's home, holds no capabilities, and cannot signal the root sandbox-tools server or reach its state in `/run/sandbox-tools`. Root runs sanitization, capture, export and the verifier.
_Avoid_: Sandbox user, non-root mode

**Capability result**:
A verifier outcome produced after an admitted arm received the task and its task-solving behavior was validly observed.
_Avoid_: Run result

**Evaluation backend**:
The local orchestration and isolation system that provisions trial environments, invokes harnesses, runs verifiers, and records evidence; it is the measuring instrument, not an experimental arm.
_Avoid_: Harness, agent

**Execution host registry**:
The reviewed, committed `hosts/<host_id>.json` entries that state each evaluation host's nonsecret identity: hostname, owner console-verified ED25519 host-key fingerprint, evaluation Docker endpoint, storage mount and data root, vault, execution root and image-store lock. A machine is an execution host only when its hostname and host key verify as an entry with a recorded fingerprint; an entry whose fingerprint is pending is registered but admits nothing. Host-key proofs, the Docker endpoint and data root behind profile observations and probes, Stage A storage policy, mount and lock, Brave's vault, and Docker selection derive from the entry; the ledger, artifact and credential-database paths an operator supplies do not.
_Avoid_: Host config, inventory, default host

**Research ledger transfer**:
The move of the conserved shared-research ledger directory to another execution host at the identical absolute path its allocation journal names: a quiescent, checksummed export on the source, a byte- and row-verified import that must pass the allocation check at the target, and retirement of the source by renaming it aside, never deleting it. _Avoid_: Ledger copy, account reset, re-provisioning

**Benchmark corpus**:
A versioned, pre-results set of frozen tasks, source and environment revisions, verifiers, exclusions, and selection rationale shared by every admitted experimental arm.
_Avoid_: Benchmark, task list, dataset

**Pilot corpus**:
A small benchmark corpus used to validate one admitted experimental arm and the end-to-end evaluation machinery before comparative experiments; its results do not support cross-arm rankings.
_Avoid_: Comparative benchmark, full benchmark

**Comparative corpus**:
A benchmark corpus selected and frozen for paired evaluation across every admitted experimental arm after the pilot corpus has validated the evaluation machinery.
_Avoid_: Pilot corpus, dataset

**Corpus freeze**:
The binding decision after which a benchmark corpus cannot be changed in place; any post-trial change requires a newly identified corpus and may not be based on capability results.

The exact archive commit and manifest, task source and text, reviewed validator, and preserved environment identities selected for a prospective task. A new validator or changed byte requires a new binding and freeze; historical task rows retain their original identities.

The execution of every block of an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze in schedule order from one ledger, advancing automatically after each clean block under the per-block supervisor and stopping fail-closed otherwise; an identity-preserving Claude enrollment renewal is a recorded operator recovery, and an offline audit of every slot precedes the seal.

# Continuous Stage A cohort

This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
prepared environment each
([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
go/no-go between blocks.

This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
in the order the tools require, up to the
owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
it. The one-task first block keeps its own
[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).

## What the harness enforces

- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
  launcher holds it.
- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
  before reservation. Serial
  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
  Claude admission and image qualification alike
  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
  `agent`, ahead of them.
  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
  ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
  The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
  execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).

## Paths and shell

Everything except the allowance steps below runs **on the execution host**,
in one zsh (or bash) shell, from the admitted staged checkout `$base/checkout`: the host must
have been re-admitted at the commit that contains this runbook's tools

## Portable preparation order

Each step consumes the previous step's output, so run them in this order. Steps
marked **owner** need the owner at the host's terminal (masked vault prompts or
an attestation); an agent never types into those prompts and never writes an
owner record. No step before the launch in step 13 starts a comparative attempt.

0. Refresh the ChatGPT login (**owner**), then re-admit the execution host at
   the final commit. When the cohort moves to another host (attempt 7: asrock
   to Alexander), first move the shared-research ledger and its allocation
   receipt with the [ledger transfer runbook](research-ledger-transfer.md),
   and once the new host is admitted, retire any earlier Stage A ledger it
   still holds ([below](#retire-an-earlier-ledger-on-a-newly-used-host-owner-decision)).
1. The archive allowance ([above](#research-allowance)) and its top-up
   ([above](#research-allowance-top-up-4)) are already applied; they travel
   with the ledger.
2. Export the credential leases to tmpfs (**owner**): the Brave key and every
   provider credential, in one vault unlock.
3. Fresh research and provider admission: the read-only remainder pre-check,
   deployment, Claude enrollment and quota (**owner**), Claude admission, the
   six other arms.
4. Build the plan: configuration, source arm proposal and planning values.
5. Rebind it to the fresh admission.
6. Qualify the release images with the final configuration.
7. Exercise task-input retention.
8. Assemble the unsigned candidate.
9. Owner approval of the exact candidate (**owner**).
10. Publish the approved freeze, once `frozen_at` has passed.
11. Initialize the scheduler ledger.
12. Renew the Claude enrollment for the cohort window (**owner**).
13. [Launch preflight](#pre-launch-checks) once the window opens, then
    [`systemd-run`](#launch).

Merge nothing to `main` from step 0 until the launch. Host admission, Claude
admission (step 3) and the plan build (step 4) fetch `origin/main`, so they
need Gitea to answer, and they refuse with `source branch moved from selected
commit` once `main` has moved past the admitted commit. After a merge in that
window, steps 3 and 4 can no longer run or be rerun at the admitted commit;
recover by re-admitting at the new commit (step 0).
After the launch, merges never block the cohort or a reboot recovery
([below](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)).

The provider-free [systemd rehearsal](#required-systemd-rehearsal) has no
inputs from these steps; complete it before step 9, since its result is part
of what the owner approves.

# Domain docs

Single-context layout: one `CONTEXT.md` at the repository root; decisions
that are hard to reverse join the authoritative documents under
`docs/authoritative/`, following that directory's existing organization.

Consumer rules: read `CONTEXT.md` before naming tests, interfaces, or
spec/ticket titles so vocabulary matches the domain language ("experimental
arm", "standard arm", and friends — avoid the terms CONTEXT.md marks as
_Avoid_). Consult the authoritative documents touching an area before
changing behavior they decided.
# Issue tracker: Gitea via the gitea-issues skill

Issues live in this repository's Gitea instance. All issue and pull-request
operations go through the bundled `gitea-issues` skill helpers
(`gitea.py issue …`, `gitea.py epic …`, `gitea.py pr …`), never hand-written
API calls.

## Workflow

- A placed actionable issue starts with `Parent: #N <title>`: the roadmap for a
  top-level entry, or its epic for a child. This is a navigation copy of the
  priority list, which remains authoritative. In this repository's legacy
  relationship mode, update the line with a guarded body edit when placement
  changes; unplaced issues and the roadmap have no `Parent:` line.
- After that line, actionable issue bodies use the four sections in
  `.gitea/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md`: `## Problem`, `## Scope`,
  `## Acceptance Criteria`, and `## Dependencies`. Keep current decisions in

1	# Continuous Stage A cohort
2	
3	This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
4	reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
5	admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
6	([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
7	For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
8	prepared environment each
9	([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
10	that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
11	first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
12	go/no-go between blocks.
13	
14	This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
15	execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
16	in the order the tools require, up to the
17	owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
18	it. The one-task first block keeps its own
19	[runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).
20	
21	## What the harness enforces
22	
23	- **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
24	  record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
25	  disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
26	- **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
27	  per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
28	  clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
29	  appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
30	  while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
31	  exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
32	- **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
33	  progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
34	  ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
35	  completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
36	  launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
37	  launcher holds it.
38	- **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
39	  An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
40	  chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
41	  stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
42	  rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
43	- **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
44	  vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
45	  that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
46	  tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
47	  token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
48	- **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
49	  launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
50	  boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
51	  token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
52	  service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
53	  down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
54	  stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
55	  past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
56	- **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
57	  cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
58	  a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
59	  a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
60	  recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
61	  native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
62	  before reservation. Serial
63	  owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
64	  makes the checked slot the one reserved.
65	- **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
66	  archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
67	  top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
68	  ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
69	  [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
70	  admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
71	  Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
72	  the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
73	  to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
74	  of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
75	  charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
76	  `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
77	  (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
78	  never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
79	  freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
80	  as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
81	- **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
82	  `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
83	  ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
84	  The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
85	- **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
86	  `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
87	  Claude admission and image qualification alike
88	  ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
89	  Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
90	  refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
91	  home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
92	  with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
93	  can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
94	  and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
95	  agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
96	  handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
97	  `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
98	  account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
99	  `agent`, ahead of them.
100	  An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
101	  it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
102	- **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
103	  environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
104	  installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
105	  ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
106	  Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
107	  exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
108	  checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
109	  Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
110	  within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
111	  ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
112	  The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
113	  execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).

1345	### Required systemd rehearsal
1346	
1347	The automatic advance depends on systemd behaviour that has not been rehearsed
1348	on the evaluation host: a unit with `Restart=on-success`,
1349	`SuccessExitStatus=3` and `RestartPreventExitStatus=3` must restart after exit
1350	`0`, stop after exit `3`, stop without restart after a failure, and apply
1351	`RuntimeMaxSec` afresh to every restarted block. Rehearse it provider-free with
1352	a stub before approving the launch configuration:
1353	
1354	```sh
1355	rehearsal="$(mktemp -d)"
1356	started=$(date +%s)
1357	cat > "$rehearsal/block.sh" <<'EOF'
1358	#!/bin/sh
1359	count=$(cat "$1/count" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
1360	count=$((count + 1))
1361	echo "$count" > "$1/count"
1362	date -u +%s >> "$1/starts"
1363	sleep 3
1364	[ "$count" -lt 3 ] && exit 0
1365	exit 3
1366	EOF
1367	chmod 0700 "$rehearsal/block.sh"
1368	systemd-run --user --service-type=exec --unit=stage-a-cohort-rehearsal \
1369	  --property=Restart=on-success --property=RestartSec=2 \
1370	  --property=SuccessExitStatus=3 --property=RestartPreventExitStatus=3 \
1371	  --property=RuntimeMaxSec=5 /bin/sh "$rehearsal/block.sh" "$rehearsal"
1372	sleep 25
1373	cat "$rehearsal/count"
1374	journalctl --user -u stage-a-cohort-rehearsal --since "@$started" -o cat --no-pager | grep -c 'Scheduled restart job'
1375	systemctl --user show stage-a-cohort-rehearsal -p LoadState
1376	```

1380	block exited `3` the unit stopped without a restart, and systemd unloaded the
1381	finished transient unit (so `show` reports defaults for its other properties).

1389	sleep 12

1462	### Keep the host unchanged while the cohort runs
1463	
1464	Every dispatch re-checks the admitted host before reserving: kernel release,
1465	system libraries, the `uv`, `npm`, `bwrap` and `docker` binaries, the Docker
1466	server, the staged checkout's Python and Node trees, a synchronized clock and
1467	free space on the ledger, artifact, vault and Docker filesystems. A change
1468	stops the cohort at its next slot with nothing reserved. Until the cohort is
1469	sealed:
1470	
1471	- install no package updates (`pacman -Syu`, Docker, kernel) and change no
1472	  file in the staged checkout;
1473	- do not reboot. A reboot removes both credential leases; if one happens,
1474	  re-export them (step 2) before resuming;
1475	- keep the desktop logged out: the verifier needs its memory;
1476	- leave the vault unchanged. A new ChatGPT login changes the admitted vault
1477	  digest; an expiring ChatGPT token stops the cohort before a GPT slot, and
1478	  recovery is retirement and re-admission. The token refreshed in step 0 lasts
1479	  10 days.
1480	
1481	Every dispatch, and the lease re-export after a reboot (step 2), also
1482	requires the staged checkout to be the admitted commit, clean, with the
1483	expected origin URL, at its recorded path. Both check this locally and never
1484	fetch origin, so after the launch neither a Gitea outage nor a merge to `main`
1485	stops the cohort or blocks a reboot recovery.
1486	
1487	Cohorts admitted at an older commit fetch `origin/main` and require it to
1488	still be the admitted commit:
1489	
1490	- without `agent_harness_evals/host_dispatch.py`, before every reservation.
1491	  While such a cohort runs, merge nothing to `main`, and expect a stop whenever
1492	  Gitea does not answer within 60 s: its nightly database backup runs at
1493	  midnight ([stop and resume](#stop-and-resume));
1494	- with `host_dispatch.py` but without its `admitted_profile`, only in the lease
1495	  re-export. A merge to `main` does not stop such a cohort, but after the next
1496	  reboot its leases cannot be re-exported and the attempt must be retired.
1497	  Merge nothing to `main` while it runs.

1511	## Stop and resume
1512	
1513	A failed unit (`Result` other than `success`) has stopped the cohort
1514	fail-closed. Retain the ledger, `$artifacts`, `${artifacts}.task-inputs`, the
1515	unit journal and image state. Diagnose the named error before anything else:
1516	
1517	- **`unreconciled active attempt`**: an attempt was in flight or uncertain. It is
1518	  never replayed. Reconcile it only through an existing, reviewed scheduler
1519	  recovery with owner disposition; this runbook authorizes none.
1520	- **`Claude enrollment cannot cover its turn`**: the next Claude slot was not
1521	  reserved because no receipt covered it. Record a renewal (below), then
1522	  resume. Renewing ahead of expiry avoids this stop.
1523	- **`cohort progress chain is broken` or `scheduler ledger was reset or
1524	  rewritten`**: the evidence changed outside the launcher. Stop and obtain an
1525	  owner disposition; never edit records to resume.
1526	- **`live research remainder cannot cover`**: the conserved shared account
1527	  cannot cover the unfinished attempts' whole workflow allowances. Nothing was
1528	  reserved. Stop; the allowance changes only by a new owner decision, never by
1529	  borrowing or resetting usage.
1530	- **A native sandbox failure** does not stop the cohort. Any error from the
1531	  sandbox while the agent's process is being started or streamed is recorded
1532	  as the slot's `infrastructure_failed` outcome, and the block continues. The
1533	  freeze allows one attempt per slot, so that slot is terminal; it is not
1534	  rerun. The error code is:
1535	  - `native_process_lost` when the sandbox-tools server no longer knows the
1536	    process. It answers `No job found with pid N`, or stops answering after a
1537	    timed-out poll is re-polled twice. Attempt 6 showed the agent can still be
1538	    running then: the server had been replaced, which starts a new server with
1539	    no jobs and leaves the old server's jobs running as orphans. What replaced
1540	    it is unconfirmed.
1541	  - `native_sandbox_failed` for any other error, such as `exec_remote`
1542	    failing at start or the server failing to restart.
1543	
1544	  Before the error is recorded, a probe run with a plain `docker exec` keeps
1545	  the server's state, then stops every process the agent started: everything
1546	  in the container started since the job, or since the current server after a
1547	  failed start, except pid 1 and the servers. Find both under
1548	  `adapter.diagnostics.native_process.sandbox_failure` in the attempt's
1549	  `native/native.json`:
1550	  - `server_at_start` is the server and job identified when the job started.
1551	  - `server` gives whether that server is still `alive`, the `current` one,
1552	    whether it was `replaced`, the state directory's `entries`, and the
1553	    bounded tail of `server-stderr.log`.
1554	  - `stop` gives the `epoch` the agent was dated from, how many processes were
1555	    `signalled`, any `remaining`, `confirmed`, and the `reason` when nothing
1556	    could be signalled: no start to date the agent, or not a container.
1557	
1558	  The outcome is recorded only once the stop is `confirmed`; Claude Code's
1559	  driver cleanup must also confirm its own process group. An agent that
1560	  cannot be confirmed stopped, or an outcome whose sandbox cleanup or research
1561	  accounting cannot be confirmed, leaves the attempt uncertain and stops the
1562	  cohort as above. `poll_timeouts` counts the timed-out polls the stream
1563	  re-polled; the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll itself.
1564	- **An adapter setup failure before provider contact** does not stop the
1565	  cohort either
1566	  ([ADR 0034](../authoritative/adr/0034-record-pre-contact-adapter-setup-failures-and-qualify-every-adapters-workspace-steps.md)).
1567	  When an adapter records its own setup or admission failure and no tool
1568	  inventory was approved, no provider request was forwarded. The slot
1569	  records `infrastructure_failed` with the adapter's code, and the block
1570	  continues; that slot is terminal. Find the code and message under
1571	  `adapter.failure` in the attempt's `native/native.json`. Codes include:
1572	  - `initial_workspace_unobservable`: OpenCode could not list the starting
1573	    workspace, without its declared dependency paths, within 10 seconds and
1574	    below Inspect's exec output limit. Image qualification checks this
1575	    listing for every task, so it should not recur on a qualified release.
1576	    Compare the task's `adapter_workspace.opencode` qualification record with
1577	    the workspace in the evidence.
1578	  - `agent_handover_failed`: the agent user could not be given the harness's
1579	    home (Codex or OpenCode).
1580	  - `setup_timed_out`: a Codex or OpenCode setup step outlived its own limit.
1581	    It is not the task's wall-time timeout.
1582	  - `setup_failed`: the sandbox failed under another setup step.
1583	  - `harness_installation_failed`, `authentication_failed` and the other
1584	    adapter setup codes.
1585	
1586	  An unadmitted or changed tool inventory is not a setup failure. It still
1587	  stops the cohort as `unadmitted native tool inventory`, or with the
1588	  adapter's message, and the attempt is uncertain as above. So does an
1589	  adapter failure that names no kind and code.
1590	- **A watchdog timeout or other crash**: inspect the attempt directory and
1591	  journal; an attempt that started is uncertain and is handled as above.
1592	- **`private runtime research credential required` or `must be the volatile
1593	  tmpfs lease`**: the tmpfs lease is gone, normally after a reboot. Re-export it
1594	  ([step 2](#2-export-the-credential-leases-to-tmpfs-owner)) before
1595	  resuming; never place the key anywhere else.
1596	
1597	- **`TimeoutExpired` from `git fetch --no-tags origin refs/heads/main`**
1598	  (only the older cohorts that fetch origin, see
1599	  [above](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)): Gitea did not answer
1600	  within 60 s, typically during its midnight backup. Nothing was reserved.
1601	  Once `git -C "$checkout" ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` answers,
1602	  `systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit"` and resume as below; after a lease
1603	  re-export's timeout, rerun the export first.
1604	- **`source branch moved from selected commit`** (the same cohorts, from a
1605	  dispatch or a lease re-export): something was merged to `main`. Every later

1609	- **`host admission rejected (TimeoutError)`**: before reserving, a probe hit

1621	  timeout 30 git -C "$archive_root" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no && echo 'archive checkout answers'

1634	
1635	- **A slot rehearsal failure** (for example `provider credential lease is
1636	  missing`, `Codex ChatGPT access token expires before the pilot's worst-case
1637	  attempt window`, `fresh Max 5x evaluation-only enrollment evidence
1638	  required`, or a research service or sandbox error): the slot is still
1639	  pending and nothing was reserved. Fix the cause (re-export the leases after
1640	  a reboot, record a Claude renewal), then resume. An expired ChatGPT token
1641	  needs a new login, which changes the vault the host was admitted with:
1642	  retire the attempt and re-admit.
1643	
1644	Resuming is a recovery, not a new approval. It must use the same freeze,
1645	configuration, ledger, admission, approval, host profile and artifact root,
1646	and it starts the same unit command above. A failed transient unit stays
1647	loaded and `systemd-run` refuses its name: clear it first with
1648	`systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit"`, then run the [launch](#launch) blocks. Each invocation re-authenticates
1649	every input and the progress chain before it reserves anything; a changed
1650	configuration or ledger is rejected. Never delete, reset or reinitialize the
1651	ledger, and never move the artifact root of an attempt that will resume.
1652	After any reboot, re-export the leases (step 2) before the resumed unit starts.
1653	
1654	When the cohort is stopped for good (an owner decision not to resume), remove
1655	the leases so the keys leave the host's memory:
1656	
1657	```sh
1658	providers="$(dirname "$lease")/stage-a-provider-credentials"
1659	rm -- "$lease" "$providers"/* && rmdir -- "$providers" "$(dirname "$lease")" && echo 'credential leases removed'
1660	```
1661	
1662	### Retire a stopped attempt (owner decision)
1663	
1664	An attempt whose launched cohort stopped with an uncertain reservation cannot
1665	resume, and a new attempt needs a new freeze and an empty ledger at the
1666	admitted path. With the owner's recorded decision to start a new attempt (for
1667	example after a code fix that needs re-admission), retire the stopped attempt
1668	before re-admitting, and after any on-host rehearsal of the fix. Use the stopped attempt's `attempt` and admitted profile
1669	in [Paths and shell](#paths-and-shell), from its still-admitted staged
1670	checkout: before step 0 moves the checkout. The block requires the unit to
1671	have no running process and clears it. It moves the ledger into the attempt's
1672	own directory first: the image store refuses any change while the ledger at the
1673	admitted path still holds an attempt, and a retired ledger no longer governs
1674	the store. It then releases the attempt's task image, moves the artifact root
1675	and its task-input store there too (never deleting anything) and recreates an
1676	empty artifact root:
1677	
1678	```sh
1679	contract_digest=$(.venv/bin/python -B -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["contract_digest"])' "$profile")
1680	unit="agent-evals-host-$(printf '%s' "${contract_digest#sha256:}" | cut -c1-24)"
1681	retired="$cohort/retired"
1682	if test "$(systemctl --user show "$unit" -p MainPID --value)" = 0; then
1683	  { systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true; } \
1684	    && mkdir -m 700 "$retired" \
1685	    && mv -- "$ledger" "$retired/scheduler.json" \
1686	    && .venv/bin/python -B scripts/stage_a_storage.py release "$ledger" \
1687	    && mv -- "$artifacts" "$retired/live" \
1688	    && { test ! -e "${artifacts}.task-inputs" || mv -- "${artifacts}.task-inputs" "$retired/live.task-inputs"; } \
1689	    && mkdir -m 700 "$artifacts" \
1690	    && sha256sum "$retired/scheduler.json" \
1691	    && echo "attempt $attempt retired to $retired"
1692	else
1693	  echo "stop: $unit is running; observe it, never retire a running attempt"
1694	fi
1695	```
1696	
1697	Expected: the release JSON (`status=released`), the retired ledger's SHA-256
1698	and `attempt N retired to …`; any refusal stops the chain where it failed and
1699	prints no `retired` line. If an [on-host rehearsal](#0-re-admit-the-execution-host-at-the-final-commit)
1700	is planned, run it first: it needs the attempt's task image, which retirement
1701	releases. Record the SHA-256, the owner's decision and the
1702	reason on the cohort's issue. The retired ledger is never resumed, edited or
1703	reused; its stopped slot runs again as a fresh slot of the next attempt's
1704	freeze. The next attempt uses `attempt=N+1` and starts at step 0.
1705	
1706	### Retire an earlier ledger on a newly used host (owner decision)
1707	
1708	A host that ran Stage A before may still hold that work's ledger at the
1709	admitted path, with its artifact root and image-store state beside it:
1710	Alexander holds the 2026-09-24 first-block ledger (175 slots, 7 terminal, no
1711	reservation), its `live` artifacts, and a `.stage-a-image-state.json` whose
1712	image was already released. The second [Paths and shell](#paths-and-shell)
1713	block refuses a present ledger (`no scheduler ledger yet`). The earlier image
1714	state names the daemon and storage policy that host had then, so after a
1715	change of daemon (Alexander's move to the dedicated daemon) it no longer
1716	validates: `stage_a_storage.py release` refuses it, and so does the cohort's
1717	first image preparation. It is retired with the ledger instead of released,
1718	and only when it records `released`, which proves the earlier daemon holds no
1719	task image of that work.
1720	
1721	With the owner's recorded decision, after the host is admitted at the final
1722	commit, run this after the first Paths and shell block and before the second.
1723	It moves the ledger, the image state and the artifact root into their own
1724	directory, never deleting anything; `label` names the earlier work:
1725	
1726	```sh
1727	label=first-block-220
1728	retired="$base/state/stage-a/retired-$label"
1729	image_state="$(dirname "$ledger")/.stage-a-image-state.json"
1730	if ! test -e "$retired" && test -f "$ledger" \
1731	    && test -z "$(systemctl --user list-units --no-legend 'agent-evals-host-*' --state=active)" \
1732	    && { test ! -e "$image_state" || .venv/bin/python -B -c 'import json,sys; sys.exit(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["status"] != "released")' "$image_state"; }; then
1733	  mkdir -m 700 "$retired" \
1734	    && mv -- "$ledger" "$retired/scheduler.json" \
1735	    && { test ! -e "$image_state" || mv -- "$image_state" "$retired/stage-a-image-state.json"; } \
1736	    && mv -- "$artifacts" "$retired/live" \
1737	    && { test ! -e "${artifacts}.task-inputs" || mv -- "${artifacts}.task-inputs" "$retired/live.task-inputs"; } \
1738	    && mkdir -m 700 "$artifacts" \
1739	    && sha256sum "$retired/scheduler.json" \
1740	    && echo "$label retired to $retired"
1741	else
1742	  echo "stop: $retired exists, no ledger at $ledger, a host unit is active, or the image state is not released; inspect before moving anything"
1743	fi
1744	```
1745	
1746	Expected: the retired ledger's SHA-256 and `<label> retired to …`. Record them
1747	and the owner's decision on the cohort's issue. An image state that is not
1748	`released` is a stop: the earlier daemon may still hold a task image, which is
1749	reconciled under that host's earlier setup, never pruned. The retired ledger
1750	is evidence of the earlier work; it is never resumed, edited or reused.
1751	
1752	### Claude enrollment renewal
1753	
1754	Step 12's confirmation covers the approved cohort window, so a cohort normally
1755	needs no further renewal. Renew only when the latest receipt would lapse
1756	before the cohort ends (for example a receipt recorded under the earlier
1757	24-hour rule), a few hours before its `valid_until`, so the windows overlap and
1758	the cohort keeps running without a stop. Print the latest receipt's expiry:
1759	
1760	```sh
1761	.venv/bin/python -B - "$configuration" "$artifacts" <<'PY'
1762	import json, sys
1763	from pathlib import Path
1764	renewals = sorted(Path(sys.argv[2]).glob('enrollment-renewals/renewal-*.json'))
1765	receipt = (json.loads(renewals[-1].read_text())['enrollment'] if renewals else
1766	           json.loads(Path(json.loads(Path(sys.argv[1]).read_text())['claude_enrollment']).read_text()))
1767	print(receipt['valid_until'])
1768	PY
1769	```
1770	
1771	The owner produces a renewed `claude-setup-token-enrollment/1` receipt and a
1772	new `owner-account-policy-confirmation/1` record whose digest is the renewed
1773	receipt's `evidence_digest` with the
1774	[step 12](#12-renew-the-claude-enrollment-for-the-cohort-window-owner) attestation, and records them
1775	with the same two commands. The renewal must keep the account, token digest,
1776	tier, `credits_enabled=false`, `evaluation_only=true` and owner; only
1777	`observed_at`, `valid_until` and `evidence_digest` may change. Its chronology
1778	must be: previous receipt's `observed_at` ≤ confirmation `recorded_at` ≤
1779	renewed `observed_at` ≤ the recording time, and renewed `valid_until` later
1780	than the previous `valid_until`. Its `observed_at` should not be later than the
1781	previous `valid_until`, so the windows overlap or touch. A renewal observed
1782	after the previous receipt expired is accepted only as recovery from the
1783	fail-closed stop that expiry causes: it is rejected if any Claude turn started
1784	in the uncovered gap. Recording holds the scheduler lock, so it waits for any
1785	Claude reservation in progress and is safe while the cohort runs.
1786	
1787	Expected: `status=recorded` with a new `enrollment-renewals/renewal-NNNN.json`
1788	and `live_execution_authorized=false`. The configured receipt file is never
1789	rewritten or extended, and no reservation, refund or replay is created. A
1790	changed identity, an unbound confirmation or an invalid chronology is rejected.
1791	A running cohort picks up the renewal at its next Claude turn; after a stop,
1792	resume. Each Claude intent records the receipt it used, the worker uses exactly
1793	that receipt, and the next progress record binds every renewal.
1794	
1795	## Audit and seal
1796	
1797	After the unit completes, run the offline cohort audit in a fresh invocation of
1798	the admitted supervisor unit, as in the first-block runbook, with:
1799	
1800	```sh
1801	"$checkout/.venv/bin/python" -B "$checkout/scripts/audit_stage_a_first_block.py" cohort-audit \
1802	  --freeze "$freeze" --configuration "$configuration" --ledger "$ledger" \
1803	  --admission-directory "$admission" --approval "$approval" \
1804	  --host-profile "$profile" --trusted-host-digest "$trusted_host_digest" \
1805	  --artifacts "$artifacts"
1806	```
1807	
1808	Expected: `status=passed`, `slots` equal to the frozen schedule, and an
1809	immutable `$artifacts/cohort-audit.json`. The audit reconstructs every slot with
1810	the first-block evidence checks and the unchanged secret scan, verifies the
1811	task-input store, requires every block's progress record in schedule order, and
1812	binds each renewal to the Claude turns it covered (renewal `observed_at` ≤
1813	`recorded_at` ≤ the covered intent), with the same overlap and gap rules as
1814	recording. Every renewal must be recorded between the approved freeze's
1815	`frozen_at` and the audit, so step 12's pre-launch renewal (recorded after
1816	publication, which follows `frozen_at`) is part of the cohort and one recorded
1817	before the freeze is refused; one that no Claude turn used (for example a second early renewal,
1818	or one after the last Claude turn) is listed with `unused=true` and does not
1819	fail the audit. The original receipt is authenticated against admission before
1820	it anchors the renewal chain, so an overwritten receipt fails the audit.
1821	
1822	#24 then seals the cohort with the same arguments:
1823	
1824	```sh
1825	"$checkout/.venv/bin/python" -B "$checkout/scripts/seal_stage_a.py" \
1826	  --freeze "$freeze" --configuration "$configuration" --ledger "$ledger" \
1827	  --admission-directory "$admission" --approval "$approval" \
1828	  --host-profile "$profile" --trusted-host-digest "$trusted_host_digest" \
1829	  --artifacts "$artifacts"
1830	```
1831	
1832	Expected: `"status": "sealed"` and the seal path. The seal accepts the
1833	full-cohort scope only with a passing `cohort-audit.json` of the exact freeze
1834	and final ledger checkpoint, and records its `cohort_audit_digest`. It still
1835	refuses `archive-first-block/1`.
1836	
1837	Once the seal is recorded, remove the credential leases:
1838	
1839	```sh
1840	providers="$(dirname "$lease")/stage-a-provider-credentials"
1841	rm -- "$lease" "$providers"/* && rmdir -- "$providers" "$(dirname "$lease")" && echo 'credential leases removed'
1842	```
1843	
1844	## Provider-source delta
1845	
1846	This implementation changes provider-dependency modules (`host_profile.py`,
1847	`host_session.py`, `scheduler_preflight.py`, `scheduler_preflight_faults.py`,
1848	`staged_contract_v5.py`) and the v5 schema's disposition bound, and adds
1849	control modules outside the existing exemptions. The provider dependency graph
1850	itself is unchanged. `stage_a_archive_source.verify_delta` therefore rejects
1851	this source as a target: retained provider and research admission evidence
1852	cannot be carried to it and needs fresh admission, which ADR-0016 already
1853	requires. Successor host admission remains the historical 175-slot path, and
1854	a cohort-sized host is admitted directly with `execution_host_profile.py
1855	admit`. The historical image-qualification successor proof does not carry to
1856	this source either: `stage_a_image_successor_source.verify_image_successor_source`
1857	refuses it (`image qualification host implementation changed`), and the
1858	fetch-free dispatch check also changed one of that proof's pinned admission
1859	consumers, `host_successor_admission.py`. The release images are qualified
1860	afresh in [step 6](#6-qualify-the-release-images-with-the-final-configuration).
1861	
1862	The archive research allowance likewise changes `research_budget.py` and
1863	`research_allocation.py`, which the research capture and account modules
1864	import, and the v5 schema's account values. Research admission evidence
1865	captured on earlier source cannot be reused for an archive-cohort freeze; its
1866	setups would also name another account identity.
1867	
1868	## Focused review checks
1869	
1870	These tests are credential-free and start no comparative trial.
1871	`test_stage_a_archive_cohort_runbook.py` runs this runbook's tool chain, and

1876	uv tool run --from uv==0.12.9 uv run --locked pytest -q \
1877	  tests/test_stage_a_archive_configuration.py tests/test_stage_a_freeze_publication.py \

1882	  tests/test_stage_a_cohort_audit.py tests/test_stage_a_cohort_e2e.py tests/test_stage_a_preflight.py \
1883	  tests/test_task_archive.py tests/test_staged_contract_v5.py \
1884	  tests/test_stage_a_research_allocation.py tests/test_research_budget.py \
1885	  tests/test_stage_a_admission_binding.py tests/test_stage_a_numerical.py \
